newsitem.title: USA: Treasuries buoyed by Fed operation, Q2 end at noon.
newsitem.headline: Treasuries buoyed by Fed operation, Q2 end at noon.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries were higher at midday, getting support in otherwise uneventful trade from a coupon pass by the Federal Reserve and by end-of-quarter position squaring, analysts said.
"That is tempering the bears and helping hold the market in," said Josh Stiles, senior bond strategist at I.D.E.A. Inc.
The bond hesitated before edging up to a 98-13/32 session high in the wake of the Fed operation.
Analysts said that although traders may have been surprised by the timing of the permanent reserve injection, they seemed to wait for the market's reaction before buying.
At midday, the 30-year bond was up 11/32, standing at 98-11/32, with a yield of 6.75 percent. The 10-year note was up 6/32 at 101-5/32, yielding 6.46 percent.

Stiles said a firm dollar also helped the market and said there could be a little more buying on Monday, predicting that some index funds playing it "right by the book" to the very end will perform a final quarter-end window dressing.

Treasuries spent most of the morning treading water -- despite further data confirming the recent strength of the U.S. economy -- ahead of next week's Federal Open Market Committee Meeting and the first reading on data from June.

"We're awaiting data next week which are more timely, bearing on June trends," said Lee Youngdahl, bond market analyst at Aubrey G. Lanston and Co Inc. "So there is really not a lot of reaction going on, we're quite rangebound and quite uninspired."
Bonds shrugged off as old news the third and final revision to first-quarter Gross Domestic Product, which added another 0.1 percent to the already frothy rate of growth.
The Commerce Department said GDP rose at an annualized rate of 5.9 percent in the first quarter, up from a preliminary 5.8 percent.
The market also reacted little to a report showing a big upward revision to the June Consumer Confidence Index released by the University of Michigan.
The final sentiment reading of 104.5 was above the preliminary reading of 103.2 for June, and was also above expectations of 103.5.

"The only thing now we have to wait for is the upcoming week when the Open Market Committee is going to pronounce what it's decided," said William Griggs, managing director at Griggs and Santow Inc. "The market fully believes they aren't going to do anything."

The two-day FOMC meeting starts Tuesday. In addition, several important economic reports, including Tuesday's National Association of Purchasing Management index for June, and June payrolls data on Thursday, will be compressed in a shortened week, due to the Fourth of July holiday on Friday.
"You'll see some squaring up at end of Thursday but there is a lot of wood to chop in the meantime," Youngdahl said.
In other trade, the five-year note was up 5/32 at 99-22/32 to yield 6.32 percent.
In bills, the three-month was up one basis point at 5.00 percent and the six-month was flat at 5.03 percent in early afternoon trade.
